How the values are worked out

Value vs price. Value comes from the latest reported numbers only (no targets, no forecasts) and is compared with today's price: owner earnings at today's metal prices × 12 / 15 / 25 + net cash for producers and royalties, NAV for developers and physical holders, and for growth companies the yearly growth the price needs (5 years, 15x exit, 10% US / 12% India). Profit vs price. Growth in profit and in the share price over about three years; the grade says whether the P/E fell (A ≤ −25%, B ≤ 0) or rose (C ≤ +33%, D above). Rules. Tier A: start at or below the 15x value, add at or below 12x. Tiers B and C: buy only with a 20% margin at 12x and AISC ≤ 60% of spot, or ≤ 0.8× NAV (0.85× physical). Red = ≥ 25x, ≥ 1.5× NAV or no valid value. Before buying: price vs 200-day average (below = buy in thirds), RSI/MACD; sell puts at 12x. Profit growth vs price growth

At a glance: A 6 · B 2 · C 5 · D 3 · n/m 10. Profits outran the price and cheap on value (A/B + green): NEM. Price outran profits and expensive (D + red): WPM, CGN.

How to read it. Growth is a yearly rate over about three years: for Indian companies Screener.in's compounded figures (net profit, latest three financial years; share price over three years); for the rest, Yahoo Finance statements from the financial year about three years back to the latest twelve months (diluted EPS, so buybacks and new shares count). P/E change = ((1 + price growth) ÷ (1 + profit growth)) ^ years − 1: negative means the share is cheaper relative to profits than at the start. Grade: A = P/E fell 25% or more · B = fell up to 25% · C = rose up to a third · D = rose more than a third · n/m = not comparable. Prices are in the exchange's currency; sales and profits as reported (m = millions, cr = crore). Profits include one-offs – check large jumps in the filing. A rising metal price lifts miners' profits faster than their prices (most gold miners grade A now); if the metal falls, profits fall faster too.

How the value is calculated

  1. No earnings yet: value comes from the feasibility study – the after-tax NPV at several metal prices.
  2. Read the NPV at today's metal price (straight line between the study's cases), × ownership.
  3. Add cash, subtract debt, divide by shares = NAV per share. The study NPV is a ceiling, not a floor.
  4. Rule: BUY ≤ 0.8× NAV, WATCH ≤ 1.0×, HOLD ≤ 1.5×, SELL above.
Worked example: price C$9.83 ÷ NAV C$15.57 = 0.63× NAV; buy at or below C$12.45.

How the value is calculated

  1. Owner earnings = adjusted net income + D&A − sustaining capex, × periods a year.
  2. Re-price to today's metals: ounces / pounds sold × (spot − realised price) × (1 − royalty) × (1 − tax).
  3. Value = owner earnings × 12 (cautious) and × 15 (fair), plus net cash per share.
  4. Rule (tier A): start a position at or below the 15x value, add at or below 12x; AISC ≤ 60% of spot.
Worked example: (1,324 + 457 − 296) × 4 ÷ 505.5m shares = $11.75 a share; re-priced to today's metals −2.18 → $9.58. × 12 + $6.76 net cash = $121.70 (cautious); × 15 = $150.43 (fair). Price $157.69.

Checks

  • 2026 on Cameco's adjusted-earnings basis (share-based compensation added back, Westinghouse at its 9M IFRS result annualised): about C$1.09 a share; analyst consensus C$1.08 (15 analysts). Reported 9M-2026: C$0.64.
  • 2028 on the same basis at spot US$92: about C$1.45 a share; analyst consensus for 2027 is C$2.41 (18 analysts, range 1.48–4.10). Consensus sits well above what Cameco's own contract table and outlook support – the difference would have to come from new contracts at higher prices, Westinghouse growth (Cameco publishes AP1000 per-project economics but no order forecast) or cheaper purchases.
  • Spot +/− US$5/lb with the 2026 contract row: earnings move the same way and by about the same amount as Cameco's own sensitivity (MD&A p. 23) – see the price_sensitivity assumptions.

Built line by line from the company's outlook, capital plan and contract table (sources in the assumptions below). The headline value stays on reported results. Green: at or above today's price.

How the value is calculated

  1. Owner earnings = adjusted net income + D&A − sustaining capex, × periods a year.
  2. No re-pricing to spot: earnings stay at the company's own realised prices – Cameco sells uranium mostly under long-term contracts.
  3. Value = owner earnings × 12 (cautious) and × 15 (fair), plus net cash per share.
  4. Rule (tier A): start a position at or below the 15x value, add at or below 12x; AISC ≤ 60% of spot.
Worked example: (279 + 150 + 203 − 242) × 4/3 ÷ 435.5m shares in CADm, converted to USD = $0.86 a share. × 12 − $0.23 net debt = $10.04 (cautious); × 15 = $12.61 (fair). Price $63.04.

Assumptions and data notes

  • Price cases only (headline value unchanged): realised price from Cameco's table of expected realized price at each spot price, 2028 row (Q3-2026 MD&A, 30 Sep 2026) - the table is Cameco's, not a forecast; it covers only contracts finalised at 30 Sep 2026
  • Price cases: 28m lb a year sold (average committed deliveries 2026-2030, MD&A p. 24); 3m lb a year bought at spot (2026 outlook: market purchases up to 3m lb). JV Inkai purchases (4.2m lb) left out - their higher cost comes back as Cameco's share of Inkai earnings
  • Price cases: royalty 7.7% = royalties / uranium revenue, 9M-2026 (145.4 / 1,888); the Saskatchewan profit royalty makes the rate on extra revenue higher, so the upside cases are a little generous. Tax 25% = income tax / earnings before tax, 9M-2026 (65 / 263)
  • Check (MD&A p. 23): with the 2026 row, 30m lb sold, spot US$89.50 and 1.35 USDCAD, these inputs give revenue +$10m / -$10m and adjusted net earnings -$8m / +$8m for spot +/- US$5/lb; Cameco reports +$6m / -$11m and -$7m / +$4m. Right direction; the fall is overstated (floors and inventory accounting are not modelled)
  • Owner earnings, 9M-2026 (Q3-2026 MD&A): adjusted net earnings 279 + addbacks 150.5 + D&A 203 − sustaining and capacity-replacement capex 242, × 4/3
  • Capex 242 = 9M additions to property, plant and equipment 321.5 × 75% – the sustaining + capacity replacement share of the 2026 plan (387.5 of 515, 2025 annual MD&A); growth capex left out
  • Addbacks 150.5 = Westinghouse restated +197, less share-based compensation −46.5. Westinghouse sits in adjusted net earnings at about −59 (IFRS net loss −80, mostly amortisation of the purchase price, plus Cameco's adjustments +21); its owner earnings are adjusted EBITDA 427 − incentive plan 50 − other expenses 23 − net finance costs 135 − sustaining capex 81 (9M capex 146 × the 2026 plan's sustaining share 100 / 180) = 138, tax about nil. Share-based compensation 62 (added back in adjusted net earnings) is a real cost: −62 × (1 − 25%)
  • Forward 2028: uranium unit cost held at the 2026 guidance (C$67–70/lb, with purchases at about C$110/lb – more if spot stays near US$92); fuel services, administration, exploration, R&D, finance costs, Inkai and Westinghouse held at 2026 levels – Cameco gives no 2028 outlook for them. 28m lb = average committed deliveries 2026–2030

How the value is calculated

  1. Owner earnings = adjusted net income (royalty and streaming companies have no meaningful capex), × periods a year.
  2. Re-price to today's metals: ounces / pounds sold × (spot − realised price) × (1 − royalty) × (1 − tax).
  3. Value = owner earnings × 12 (cautious) and × 15 (fair), plus net cash per share.
  4. Rule (tier A): start a position at or below the 15x value, add at or below 12x; AISC ≤ 60% of spot.
Worked example: (364) × 4 ÷ 193.3m shares = $7.54 a share; re-priced to today's metals −1.16 → $6.38. × 12 + $6.37 net cash = $82.98 (cautious); × 15 = $102.13 (fair). Price $233.74.

How the value is calculated

  1. No earnings yet: value comes from the feasibility study – the after-tax NPV at several metal prices.

  3. Add cash, subtract debt, divide by shares = NAV per share. The study NPV is a ceiling, not a floor.
